entities.title: Version numbers
entities.summary: version.test.sh runs version.sh in a throwaway repository with release tags.
criteria: With no tag, a patch bump gives v0.0.1
Tags sort as versions, so the next patch after v1.2.9, v1.2.10 and v1.10.0 is v1.10.1; minor and major bump likewise
bump none gives no tag, version 0.0.0-dev and no publish; a pushed vX.Y.Z tag is taken as it is
A pushed tag that is not vX.Y.Z, and an unknown bump, are refused
notChecked: set-version.sh has no test of its own; only shellcheck runs on it in CI.

entities.title: Formula and bottle
entities.summary: formula.test.sh runs formula.sh and bottle.sh and checks their output under a stand-in Homebrew Formula class, for both CPU types.
criteria: Bad arguments are refused and write nothing
One formula, valid Ruby, with the release's url, version, sha256, license, depends_on :macos and a description

It installs the five binaries, both gzipped indexers and the placeholder; the one post_install step, run for real against a fake keg and a fake uname, expands the indexer for arm64 and for x64 and leaves no temporary file
Its test block runs one command per binary, and release.yml builds every binary
One reproducible bottle with exactly the expected files, the binaries and the placeholder mode 0755 and root-owned, the placeholder identical to the formula's
With the bottle, the formula's bottle block matches its name and checksum; a missing bottle or bottle folder is refused
notChecked: Homebrew itself: the stand-in is not Homebrew, and nothing has pulled a real bottle until a tag runs.
What the binaries really print for their version: the stand-in answers for them.

entities.title: Signing and notarization
entities.summary: sign-and-notarize.test.sh runs sign-and-notarize.sh against recording stand-ins for security, codesign, xcrun and ditto.
criteria: Without secrets it warns, runs no tool and succeeds; with REQUIRE_SIGNING=true it fails, naming only the missing secrets
With every secret it signs each binary with hardened runtime and a timestamp, verifies it, notarizes with the API key and waits, and removes the keychain
A rejected or failed notarization fails the run, prints Apple's log when there is a submission, and still removes the keychain
A certificate that is not a Developer ID Application one fails before anything is signed
Missing arguments are a usage error

checks.description: After a release with the secrets in place, codesign -dv on a downloaded binary shows the Developer ID authority, the runtime flag and a timestamp, and it starts from a browser download without a warning (README, Checking a signed release).

notChecked: Signing with a real certificate and notarizing with Apple: nothing has signed a real binary until a tag runs with the secrets in place.

entities.title: PGO training
entities.summary: pgo.sh has no test of its own: CI shellchecks it, and the release and zazzle-bench workflows run it, failing when training writes no profile.
criteria: It finds a training corpus or fails
Training writes at least one raw profile, and it prints PGO_CFLAGS
